import Init

/-! Candidate finite native environment supplier. Arena is a chronological append
log, not a lexical-parent chain: every appended node chooses an arbitrary older
index. Dispatch data and cell addresses are retained. No value snapshot occurs. -/
namespace YulangClosure.NativeClosureEnvironment

inductive Arena (Key Dispatch : Type) where
  | root (dispatch : Dispatch)
  | append (old : Arena Key Dispatch) (parent : Nat)
      (binder : Option (Key × Nat)) (dispatch : Dispatch)

def Arena.size : Arena K D → Nat
  | .root _ => 1
  | .append old _ _ _ => old.size + 1

inductive Valid : Arena K D → Prop where
  | root (d : D) : Valid (.root d)
  | append : Valid old → parent < old.size →
      Valid (.append old parent binder dispatch)

structure Node (K D : Type) where
  parent : Option Nat
  binder : Option (K × Nat)
  dispatch : D

def nodeAt : Arena K D → Nat → Option (Node K D)
  | .root d, i => if i = 0 then some ⟨none, none, d⟩ else none
  | .append old p b d, i =>
      if i = old.size then some ⟨some p, b, d⟩ else nodeAt old i

/-- Structurally finite evaluation. Older-index references recurse into the
old arena; Valid proves that this is precisely the native decreasing parent walk. -/
def lookup (matchesKey : K → Bool) : Arena K D → Nat → Option Nat
  | .root _, _ => none
  | .append old p b _, i =>
      if i = old.size then
        match b with
        | none => lookup matchesKey old p
        | some (key, cell) =>
            if matchesKey key then some cell else lookup matchesKey old p
      else lookup matchesKey old i

theorem lookup_old (m : K → Bool) (old : Arena K D) (p i : Nat)
    (b : Option (K × Nat)) (d : D) (hi : i < old.size) :
    lookup m (.append old p b d) i = lookup m old i := by
  simp [lookup, Nat.ne_of_lt hi]

theorem nodeAt_old (old : Arena K D) (p i : Nat)
    (b : Option (K × Nat)) (d : D) (hi : i < old.size) :
    nodeAt (.append old p b d) i = nodeAt old i := by
  simp [nodeAt, Nat.ne_of_lt hi]

theorem parent_decreases {arena : Arena K D} (valid : Valid arena)
    {i : Nat} {node : Node K D} (found : nodeAt arena i = some node)
    {p : Nat} (parent : node.parent = some p) : p < i := by
  induction valid with
  | root d =>
      simp only [nodeAt] at found
      split at found
      · cases found
        cases parent
      · cases found
  | @append old q binder dispatch hv hq ih =>
      simp only [nodeAt] at found
      split at found
      · rename_i hi
        cases found
        cases parent
        simpa [hi] using hq
      · exact ih found

/-- One append checks the newest binding before its chosen parent. These
universal equations are the nearest-match recursion, including dispatch nodes. -/
theorem lookup_new (m : K → Bool) (old : Arena K D) (p : Nat)
    (b : Option (K × Nat)) (d : D) :
    lookup m (.append old p b d) old.size =
      match b with
      | none => lookup m old p
      | some (key, cell) => if m key then some cell else lookup m old p := by
  simp [lookup]

theorem dispatch_transparent (m : K → Bool) (old : Arena K D) (p : Nat) (d : D) :
    lookup m (.append old p none d) old.size = lookup m old p := by
  simp [lookup]

def lookupKey {D : Type} [DecidableEq K] (key : K) := lookup (fun k : K => decide (k = key)) (D := D)

theorem parameter_shadows [DecidableEq K] (old : Arena K D)
    (p cell : Nat) (key : K) (d : D) :
    lookupKey key (.append old p (some (key, cell)) d) old.size = some cell := by
  simp [lookupKey, lookup]

theorem parameter_preserves [DecidableEq K] (old : Arena K D)
    (p cell : Nat) (key other : K) (d : D) (hne : key ≠ other) :
    lookupKey other (.append old p (some (key, cell)) d) old.size =
      lookupKey other old p := by
  simp [lookupKey, lookup, hne]

/-- Append histories preserve every old address, including unrelated branches. -/
inductive Extends : Arena K D → Arena K D → Prop where
  | refl : Extends a a
  | step : Extends a b → p < b.size → Extends a (.append b p binder dispatch)

theorem extends_size {a b : Arena K D} (h : Extends a b) : a.size ≤ b.size := by
  induction h with
  | refl => exact Nat.le_refl _
  | step _ _ ih => exact Nat.le_trans ih (Nat.le_succ _)

theorem lookup_history {a b : Arena K D} (h : Extends a b)
    (m : K → Bool) (i : Nat) (hi : i < a.size) : lookup m b i = lookup m a i := by
  induction h with
  | refl => rfl
  | step h hp ih =>
      rw [lookup_old _ _ _ _ _ _ (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le hi (extends_size h))]
      exact ih


theorem node_bound {arena : Arena K D} {i : Nat} {node : Node K D}
    (found : nodeAt arena i = some node) : i < arena.size := by
  induction arena with
  | root d =>
      simp only [nodeAt] at found
      split at found
      · rename_i hi
        subst i
        exact Nat.zero_lt_succ _
      · cases found
  | append old p b d ih =>
      simp only [nodeAt] at found
      split at found
      · rename_i hi
        subst i
        exact Nat.lt_succ_self _
      · exact Nat.lt_trans (ih found) (Nat.lt_succ_self _)

/-- One genuine native parent-walk step, evaluated in the same arena. -/
def step (matchesKey : K → Bool) (arena : Arena K D) (node : Node K D) : Option Nat :=
  let fallback := node.parent.bind (lookup matchesKey arena)
  match node.binder with
  | none => fallback
  | some (key, cell) => if matchesKey key then some cell else fallback

theorem lookup_node {arena : Arena K D} (valid : Valid arena)
    (matchesKey : K → Bool) {i : Nat} {node : Node K D}
    (found : nodeAt arena i = some node) : lookup matchesKey arena i = step matchesKey arena node := by
  induction valid with
  | root d =>
      simp only [nodeAt] at found
      split at found
      · cases found
        rfl
      · cases found
  | @append old p binder dispatch hv hp ih =>
      simp only [nodeAt] at found
      split at found
      · rename_i hi
        subst i
        cases found
        simp [lookup, step, Nat.ne_of_lt hp]
      · have hi := node_bound found
        rw [lookup_old matchesKey old p i binder dispatch hi, ih found]
        have fallback : node.parent.bind (lookup matchesKey old) =
            node.parent.bind (lookup matchesKey (.append old p binder dispatch)) := by
          cases he : node.parent with
          | none => rfl
          | some q =>
              simp only [Option.bind_some]
              exact (lookup_old matchesKey old p q binder dispatch
                (Nat.lt_trans (parent_decreases hv found he) hi)).symm
        simp only [step, fallback]

/-- Every valid address selects an actual node; this is independent of parent validity. -/
theorem node_exists (arena : Arena K D) (i : Nat) (hi : i < arena.size) :
    ∃ node, nodeAt arena i = some node := by
  induction arena with
  | root d =>
    have hz : i = 0 := Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero (Nat.le_of_lt_succ hi)
    subst i
    exact ⟨⟨none, none, d⟩, rfl⟩
  | append old p b d ih =>
    rcases Nat.lt_or_eq_of_le (Nat.le_of_lt_succ hi) with hlt | heq
    · obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := ih hlt
      exact ⟨n, (nodeAt_old old p i b d hlt).trans hn⟩
    · subst i
      exact ⟨⟨some p, b, d⟩, by simp [nodeAt]⟩

/-- Outer None means exhausted fuel; Some None means native lookup finished absent. -/
def walkFuel (matchesKey : K → Bool) (arena : Arena K D) : Nat → Nat → Option (Option Nat)
  | 0, _ => none
  | fuel + 1, i =>
    match nodeAt arena i with
    | none => some none
    | some node =>
      let fallback := match node.parent with
        | none => some none
        | some p => walkFuel matchesKey arena fuel p
      match node.binder with
      | none => fallback
      | some (key, cell) => if matchesKey key then some (some cell) else fallback

/-- Exact native parent walk finishes; fuel exhaustion cannot stand for absence. -/
theorem walk_complete {arena : Arena K D} (hv : Valid arena)
    (m : K → Bool) (fuel i : Nat) (hi : i < arena.size) (hf : i < fuel) :
    walkFuel m arena fuel i = some (lookup m arena i) := by
  induction fuel generalizing i with
  | zero => exact False.elim (Nat.not_lt_zero i hf)
  | succ fuel ih =>
    obtain ⟨node, hn⟩ := node_exists arena i hi
    have fallback :
        (match node.parent with
        | none => some none
        | some p => walkFuel m arena fuel p) =
        some (node.parent.bind (lookup m arena)) := by
      cases hp : node.parent with
      | none => rfl
      | some p =>
        have hpi := parent_decreases hv hn hp
        exact ih p (Nat.lt_trans hpi hi)
          (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le hpi (Nat.le_of_lt_succ hf))
    rw [lookup_node hv m hn]
    simp only [walkFuel, hn]
    cases hb : node.binder with
    | none => simpa only [step, hb] using fallback
    | some pair =>
      rcases pair with ⟨key, cell⟩
      cases hm : m key <;> simp [step, hb, hm, fallback]

theorem bounded_lookup {arena : Arena K D} (hv : Valid arena)
    (m : K → Bool) (i : Nat) (hi : i < arena.size) :
    walkFuel m arena (i + 1) i = some (lookup m arena i) :=
  walk_complete hv m (i+1) i hi (Nat.lt_succ_self i)

/-- Native extend copies the selected parent's dispatch; with_dispatch supplies
new dispatch explicitly. Invalid source indices remain outside Valid. -/
def extendNode (old : Arena K D) (parent : Nat) (key : K) (cell : Nat)
    (parentNode : Node K D) (_found : nodeAt old parent = some parentNode) : Arena K D :=
  .append old parent (some (key, cell)) parentNode.dispatch

/-- Finite store allocation retains old cells and writes the actual received
value at the new address. Rewrites remain separate current-store inputs. -/
structure Store (V : Type) where
  size : Nat
  cell : Nat → Option V

def Store.push (store : Store V) (value : V) : Store V :=
  ⟨store.size + 1, fun i => if i = store.size then some value else store.cell i⟩

theorem push_current (store : Store V) (value : V) :
    (store.push value).cell store.size = some value := by simp [Store.push]

theorem push_old (store : Store V) (value : V) (i : Nat) (hi : i < store.size) :
    (store.push value).cell i = store.cell i := by
  simp [Store.push, Nat.ne_of_lt hi]

structure Closure (Body : Type) where
  savedEnvironment : Nat
  body : Body

def capture (environment : Nat) (body : B) : Closure B := ⟨environment, body⟩
def entryEnvironment (closure : Closure B) (_caller : Nat) := closure.savedEnvironment

theorem closure_entry (saved caller : Nat) (body : B) :
    entryEnvironment (capture saved body) caller = saved := rfl

/-- The store argument is supplied at observation time, never at capture time. -/
def observe (m : K → Bool) (arena : Arena K D) (environment : Nat)
    (store : Nat → Option V) : Option V :=
  (lookup m arena environment).bind store

theorem observe_current (m : K → Bool) (arena : Arena K D) (environment cell : Nat)
    (store : Nat → Option V) (h : lookup m arena environment = some cell) :
    observe m arena environment store = store cell := by simp [observe, h]

theorem bind_observes_received [DecidableEq K] (old : Arena K D)
    (parent : Nat) (key : K) (dispatch : D) (store : Store V) (value : V) :
    observe (fun k => decide (k = key))
      (.append old parent (some (key, store.size)) dispatch) old.size
      (store.push value).cell = some value := by
  simp [observe, lookup, Store.push]

/-- Different full identities may have equal spelling; lookup retains identity. -/
example : lookupKey (1, "x")
    (.append (.append (.root ()) 0 (some ((1, "x"), 10)) ())
      1 (some ((2, "x"), 20)) ()) 2 = some 10 := rfl

example : lookupKey (1 : Nat)
    (.append (.append (.root ()) 0 (some (1, 10)) ())
      1 (some (1, 20)) ()) 2 = some 20 := rfl

/-- An unrelated latest append is not an ancestor of the chosen saved index. -/
example : lookupKey (1 : Nat)
    (.append (.append (.root ()) 0 (some (1, 10)) ())
      0 (some (2, 20)) ()) 1 = some 10 := rfl

example : observe (fun k : Nat => decide (k = 1))
    (.append (.root ()) 0 (some (1, 7)) ()) 1
    (fun _ => (none : Option Nat)) = none := rfl

example : observe (fun k : Nat => decide (k = 1))
    (.append (.root ()) 0 (some (1, 7)) ()) 1
    (fun _ => some (42 : Nat)) = some 42 := rfl

end YulangClosure.NativeClosureEnvironment

# Native closure environments, current cells and represented body realization

Status: source correspondence candidate, pending combined formal/source review.
Authors: primary /root (source/verification) and constructive author
/root/native_closure_environment_astra_r1 (formal candidate).
Baseline657d688fc022261fa1013f7eb4f2b323d6cfd4a6, research/simple-sub-intrusion.
Contract LEAN-NATIVE-CLOSURE-ENVIRONMENT-20261025/r1 SHA
2630ec7db277777bf4e0fb8e99a665cdd65d842471264a736a079c122a1f073f.
All59 pinned inputs match. Requested childAstra/medium, observedUNKNOWN.

## Authority and exact claim

The existing operational specification requires the typing context to retain
captures/shared resources (tex206), distinguishes Value formal A from Computation
formal UA (220-221), and permits a finite environment graph read as closed
substitution (258-261). This note derives the native lexical-address supplier
and uses the companion formal construction to close represented Call bodies.
It adds no language semantics, executable callable constructor or compiler change.

The environment graph, cell store and value/closure graph are distinct objects.
A closure stores an environment index, not a copy of its bound values. Environment
nodes are immutable once appended; a binder resolves to a stable cell address.
Reading that cell observes its CURRENT content, which may be uninitialized or
have been written since closure capture. A recursive local can produce a cycle
cell -> closure -> captured environment -> same cell even though environment
parent edges are acyclic. Parent acyclicity proves neither guarded value-graph
realization nor a typed store. Those original obligations remain OPEN.

For every actually generated finite environment arena and valid saved environment,
lookup terminates and returns the nearest matching full binder identity's cell.
Later arena appends do not change that old address resolution. Dispatch-only
nodes leave lexical resolution unchanged. Parameter binding shadows precisely
its full identity. Native closure entry uses the saved environment, independent
of the caller's environment except for explicitly retained dispatch/value data.
For a finite resolved layout whose current cells already have represented typed
values, the formal realization constructs the exact substitution and applies the
existing body substitution theorem. This last result remains conditional on
source layout and actual value representation/typing; it does not create those
premises from an arbitrary native store.

## All environment constructors and handle validity

Environment at machine175 retains parent Option<usize>, optional (Binder,cell)
and dispatch::State. Machine start447 creates exactly node0 with parent=None,
binder=None and default dispatch. Existing environments are never overwritten,
removed or truncated. The only production pushes are:

| Owner | New node and returned handle |
| --- | --- |
| with_dispatch2596-2599 | id=old length; parent=Some(input), binder=None, supplied dispatch; return id. |
| extend2626-2633 | id=old length; parent=Some(input), binder=Some(exact key,cell), copy parent's dispatch; return id. |
| bind2635-2638 | id=old cell length; append Some(exact ReceivedValue); then extend(input,key,id). |

All non-root environment handles originate from these returned pre-append lengths.
All other uses copy existing handles from active Evaluate state, saved frames,
Closure/Delay payloads, or use literal0 for root evaluation/initialization.
No source integer, arithmetic-derived value or caller-provided raw index becomes
an environment handle. These fields are private. Test-only hand-written machine
states are outside the production constructor induction.

Inductively, input handles are below the old arena length, and every newly
created parent is strictly below its child's new index. Earlier nodes are
unchanged. Reusing any older valid environment as parent is permitted; the graph
is not a single contiguous chain and does not require parent=child-1. Root is
parentless; every source-produced non-root node has an older parent. Thus every
lookup's followed parent chain is finite. Vector reallocation does not invalidate
index handles. Successful returned allocations are modeled; an infallible native
allocation abort is not claimed to return a recoverable error.

This is a source construction induction over the complete handle-producer set,
not an assumed arbitrary well-formed arena. The model's own append theorems
supply that invariant for all histories of such constructors, retaining dispatch
and binder/cell payloads. A malformed self-parent/cyclic arena is not a producer
result and cannot instantiate the builder theorem.

## Actual lookup, identity and module cells

Machine.lookup2585-2594 first checks the selected frame via get. If its binder
exists and the supplied predicate matches, it returns that cell immediately.
Otherwise it follows parent; a missing frame or absent parent returns None.
For generated valid environments, strict parent decrease makes the unbounded
Rust loop coincide with the finite formal lookup, including exact nearest match.
The finite bound counts environment nodes, including binderless dispatch nodes;
it does not bound later user computation or resolving value-graph cycles.

Binder at program207-211 is a tagged union of Parameter(HirParameterId),
Local(HirLocalId), and Catch(LocalSourceCatchBinderId). Name785-811 uses:

| Source resolution | Exact address lookup |
| --- | --- |
| ModuleDef(id) | definition_indices.get(full id), independent of lexical env. |
| Parameter(id) | nearest Binder::Parameter(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| Local(id) | nearest Binder::Local(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| CatchBinder(id) or CaseBinder(id) | nearest Binder::Catch(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| Imported, Unresolved, Ambiguous | no address; MissingBinding. |

HirParameterId compares source-root owner and ordinal (module1377-1408);
HirLocalId likewise retains its owner and ordinal. Catch identity additionally
retains arm_source (local_source463ff). The tags remain distinct; equal spelling,
ordinal alone, source display or hash collision is not equality. The formal key
must denote these complete identities, or an injective encoding already supplied
elsewhere. Its decidable equality is not a new spelling-based resolution policy.

Program994 and1008 set each definition index to definitions.len() immediately
before pushing that definition. Machine452 allocates exactly definitions.len()
initial cells, all None. Each stored module index is therefore in bounds; later
cell appends preserve it. Global resolution is a direct cell reference in a
resolved layout, not a fake lexical binder inserted into environment0. Missing
module ids remain failures. This address fact does not establish source-to-layout
coverage for arbitrary expressions or native cell typing.

After address resolution, Name814 reads self.cells[cell]. Missing lexical
address yields MissingBinding; present lexical cell with None yields
UninitializedBinding. Module cell None starts guarded lazy global initialization,
with a GlobalRead frame and initializer environment derived from0; repeated active
initialization yields RecursiveDefinitionInitialization. No placeholder value is
returned for an absent/uninitialized binding.

On Some(received), dispatch_name may update the copied ReceivedValue.dispatch,
then consume uses NameConsumption and may return or execute a computation.
The current-cell realization denotes the stored carrier before these operations;
address lookup transparency is not dispatch or force semantic transparency.
Neither dispatch_name nor consume writes the stored cell in this path.

## Dispatch-only nodes and error boundaries

initializer_environment2601 returns the same parent when dictionaries are absent;
otherwise it calls dispatch.initializer and appends a binderless node with the
returned state. substitute_environment2606 is a no-op if dictionaries or the
substitution are absent; otherwise it composes dispatch.substitution with the
supplied substitution and appends a binderless node. dispatch_environment2612
appends a dispatch word and likewise creates a binderless node. These wrappers
therefore preserve every lexical address on success, including nested wrappers.
Their dispatch values are retained, not erased as semantically irrelevant.

The called dispatch owner is dispatch.rs: append67, then78, initializer143,
name161. These helpers mutate their own metadata arenas/default map, never the
lexical environment nodes or cell contents. A returned error before with_dispatch
means no lexical node was appended. It does NOT mean global rollback:
initializer inserts into defaults before rejecting an existing entry, and name
can append metadata before a later allocation failure. No proof here asserts
idempotence, commutativity, freshness or observational irrelevance of those
substitutions. Their ordered semantic interpretation is a separate obligation.

## Closure capture and actual entry branches

Instruction::Lambda864-887 copies parameter, pattern flags, role, schemas, body
label and CURRENT environment into ExecutableValue::Closure. Callee1181-1200
creates the delayed argument with the CALLER environment before examining the
callee. The Closure pattern1224-1232 then binds its environment variable to the
SAVED closure environment. At1286 substitute_environment receives that saved
index and the callee ReceivedValue.dispatch; the caller's lexical environment is
not substituted for it. The delay still refers to caller environment, which is
correct argument scope, rather than a change to the closure body scope.

new_invocation runs before substitution; a later dispatch failure can retain
owner/metadata changes while body entry fails. The address theorem neither
reorders these steps nor asserts whole-machine rollback or typed error-freedom.
ReceiverReturn/ValueEntry carry the resulting saved-derived environment exactly.

| Entry branch | Lexical effect |
| --- | --- |
| Computation1316-1331 | Bind the closure parameter to the same delay handle, Computation interface, selected receiving view, dispatch=None; evaluate body without forcing it here. This branch does not inspect unit/record flags. |
| Value ordinary1440-1490 | Force argument first. After optional callback validation/view construction, bind parameter to exact returned value/view/dispatch with Value interface, then evaluate body. |
| Value unit1471-1476 | Validate actual Unit; retain saved-derived environment without a parameter binder. Failure enters no body. |
| Value record1468 / bind_record_parameter2655 | Process fields in source order; bind each field identity only when its value/default has been obtained. No whole-record parameter binder is added here. |

Optional callback_schema validation may fail before any parameter binding; on
success it changes the copied receiving view while retaining the actual value
and dispatch. The body-closing lemma must use that actual carrier's representation,
not an invented unchanged-view premise. For Computation, a represented argument
is a delay with a typed computation body; it is not an eagerly evaluated result.

bind_record_parameter first validates the argument/view and actual record. A
present field projects its view, composes its dispatch with the argument dispatch,
sets Value interface and creates a fresh parameter cell. If absent with a default,
it saves RecordDefault and evaluates the default under the environment containing
only earlier fields. On return1491, the default value/view is projected, that
field is bound, then processing resumes at index+1. Missing without default,
invalid record/view or projection failure does not silently introduce a binding.
Even empty patterns require an actual record. A default may suspend/fail/diverge;
no theorem here claims finite completion of all defaults. Repeated application
of the append lookup theorem applies to each successful field introduction.

## Cell allocation/writes and all other binder producers

There is no cell removal or index reuse. The complete production cell mutation
set found by searching every self.cells occurrence is:

| Owner | Mutation and environment relation |
| --- | --- |
| Start452 | Allocate None for every global definition. |
| begin_local2523-2526 | Append fresh None; recursive local extends env before initializer, nonrecursive does not yet extend. |
| Frame::Local1543-1560 | Write actual received carrier with Value interface; recursive env already contains the cell, nonrecursive extends now; continue the block. |
| Frame::Root1739 | Write received carrier with Value interface into scheduled definition cell. |
| Frame::GlobalRead1760 | Write received carrier with Value interface into lazily initialized global cell; then dispatch/consume a copy. |
| bind2637 | Append Some(exact supplied carrier), then extend with its fresh cell. |

The structural store theorem intentionally permits current-cell changes; it
does not claim that the runtime rewrites every initialized cell arbitrarily or
that every write preserves a source type. Recursive closure capture can occur
while its own preallocated cell is None; later initialization changes what the
same captured address reads. Before that write the partial realization must
fail; after it the same address can return the new value. The finite Call value
syntax cannot generally represent that cyclic closure graph, which remains OPEN.

All bind callers use the same constructor law: CatchReturn value arm1116;
Computation formal1316; ordinary Value formal1476; RecordDefault1494;
Case binder1699 and structural-case list1717; request payload2194 and continuation
binder2216; record field2671. The only direct extend callers besides bind are
recursive preallocation2526 and nonrecursive local completion1553. Wildcards,
unit catch payload and patterns with no binder retain the input environment.
A forwarded handler's stored environment is copied by template replay; the
reviewed template result does not mutate that environment arena or cell store.

## Formal realization application and residual source owners

The exact final APIs and their source instantiation are recorded after author
handoff and Lean verification. The required construction is partial lookup of
each resolved capture, current represented cell read, and an indexed finite
substitution whose typed indices match those reads. Only out-of-domain indices
may carry an irrelevant total-function filler. Successful realization alone
establishes value identity/coverage, not type: per-cell ValueTyped evidence must
supply the original context's declared types, including duplicate/aliased cells.
The body result then follows by the existing substituteCallComp_typed theorem,
with the constructed premise rather than an assumed typed substitution object.

Remaining owners, all primary intake:
- ENV-LAYOUT-1: actual source-resolved binder/global references and de Bruijn free
  positions for each represented body, with binder lifting and coverage.
- ENV-CELL-VALUE-1: native ReceivedValue/current cell -> represented TypedCall.Value
  and its original type; primitive literal readback is only one accepted supplier.
- ENV-GRAPH-1: guarded recursive/shared value graph realization and original typing.
- ENV-CALLABLE-1: closure as a value, full code/environment/adapter/native trace
  interpretation; current Function is outside Value and is not silently inserted.
- ENV-DISPATCH-1: source dictionary dispatch and consumption/force meaning,
  including receiving/view metadata and operation errors.

The full source-native / typed callable parent therefore remains OPEN. This
packet supplies the concrete address/current-cell/substitution mechanism and its
conditional typed body application, not arbitrary source typing or Bad exclusion.
NO_SAFE_CODE_SLICE; no confirmed runtime defect. No compiler, diagnostic,
expectation, config, native test or new production semantics change is made.

import YulangClosure.NativeClosureEnvironment
import YulangClosure.CoreSubstitution

namespace YulangClosure.CallEnvironmentRealization
open YulangClosure.Original
open YulangClosure.TypedCall
open YulangClosure.NativeClosureEnvironment

/-- A resolved lexical full identity or an already resolved global cell address.
The source resolver's coverage/accuracy is a separate premise. -/
inductive Reference (K : Type) where
  | lexical (key : K)
  | global (cell : Nat)

abbrev Layout (K : Type) := List (Reference K × Ty)

def address [DecidableEq K] (arena : Arena K D) (env : Nat) : Reference K → Option Nat
  | .lexical key => lookupKey key arena env
  | .global cell => some cell

def read [DecidableEq K] (arena : Arena K D) (env : Nat)
    (store : Nat → Option Value) (ref : Reference K) : Option Value :=
  (address arena env ref).bind store

/-- This genuinely runs the finite lookup/read sequence. Any failed read aborts. -/
def realize [DecidableEq K] (arena : Arena K D) (env : Nat)
    (store : Nat → Option Value) : Layout K → Option (List Value)
  | [] => some []
  | (ref, _) :: rest => do
      let value ← read arena env store ref
      let values ← realize arena env store rest
      pure (value :: values)

def context : Layout K → Original.Context
  | [], _ => none
  | (_, ty) :: _, 0 => some ty
  | _ :: rest, n + 1 => context rest n

/-- Filler occurs only outside the represented finite context. -/
def substitution (filler : Value) : List Value → Nat → Value
  | [], _ => filler
  | value :: _, 0 => value
  | _ :: rest, n + 1 => substitution filler rest n

inductive Captured (readValue : Reference K → Option Value) : Layout K → List Value → Prop where
  | nil : Captured readValue [] []
  | cons : readValue ref = some value → Captured readValue rest values →
      Captured readValue ((ref, ty) :: rest) (value :: values)

theorem realize_captured [DecidableEq K] (arena : Arena K D) (env : Nat)
    (store : Nat → Option Value) (layout : Layout K) (values : List Value)
    (h : realize arena env store layout = some values) :
    Captured (read arena env store) layout values := by
  induction layout generalizing values with
  | nil => simp [realize] at h; subst values; exact .nil
  | cons head rest ih =>
      rcases head with ⟨ref, ty⟩
      cases hr : read arena env store ref with
      | none => simp [realize, hr] at h
      | some value =>
          cases ht : realize arena env store rest with
          | none => simp [realize, hr, ht] at h
          | some tail =>
              simp [realize, hr, ht] at h
              subst values
              exact .cons hr (ih tail ht)

/-- Every typed free index sees a successful actual read, never the filler. -/
theorem captured_index {readValue : Reference K → Option Value}
    {layout : Layout K} {values : List Value} (h : Captured readValue layout values)
    (filler : Value) (i : Nat) (ty : Ty) (hi : context layout i = some ty) :
    ∃ ref, (ref, ty) ∈ layout ∧ readValue ref = some (substitution filler values i) := by
  induction h generalizing i with
  | nil => cases hi
  | @cons ref value rest values a hr ht ih =>
      cases i with
      | zero =>
          simp only [context, Option.some.injEq] at hi
          subst ty
          exact ⟨ref, by simp, hr⟩
      | succ i =>
          obtain ⟨r, hm, hv⟩ := ih i hi
          exact ⟨r, by simp [hm], hv⟩

/-- The per-cell typing obligation is explicit and restricted to layout entries
and successful addresses/current reads. Arbitrary stores need not be typed. -/
def CellsTyped [DecidableEq K] (arena : Arena K D) (env : Nat)
    (store : Nat → Option Value) (layout : Layout K) : Prop :=
  ∀ ref ty, (ref, ty) ∈ layout → ∀ cell value,
    address arena env ref = some cell → store cell = some value →
    ValueTyped emptyContext value ty

theorem successful_read_typed [DecidableEq K] {arena : Arena K D} {env : Nat}
    {store : Nat → Option Value} {layout : Layout K} (hc : CellsTyped arena env store layout)
    {ref : Reference K} {ty : Ty} (hm : (ref, ty) ∈ layout)
    {value : Value} (hr : read arena env store ref = some value) :
    ValueTyped emptyContext value ty := by
  cases ha : address arena env ref with
  | none => simp [read, ha] at hr
  | some cell =>
      have hs : store cell = some value := by simpa [read, ha] using hr
      exact hc ref ty hm cell value ha hs

theorem realized_substitution_typed [DecidableEq K] {arena : Arena K D} {env : Nat}
    {store : Nat → Option Value} {layout : Layout K} {values : List Value}
    (success : realize arena env store layout = some values)
    (cells : CellsTyped arena env store layout) (filler : Value) :
    ∀ i ty, context layout i = some ty →
      ValueTyped emptyContext (substitution filler values i) ty := by
  intro i ty hi
  obtain ⟨ref, hm, hr⟩ := captured_index
    (realize_captured arena env store layout values success) filler i ty hi
  exact successful_read_typed cells hm hr

/-- Parent application: actual successful capture construction supplies the
existing substitution theorem, including its bind and request lifting cases. -/
theorem close_body [DecidableEq K] {arena : Arena K D} {env : Nat}
    {store : Nat → Option Value} {layout : Layout K} {values : List Value}
    (success : realize arena env store layout = some values)
    (cells : CellsTyped arena env store layout) (filler : Value)
    {body : TypedCall.Comp} {result : Ty} (typed : TypedCall.CompTyped (context layout) body result) :
    TypedCall.CompTyped emptyContext (substituteCallComp (substitution filler values) body) result :=
  substituteCallComp_typed typed (realized_substitution_typed success cells filler)

def parameterSubstitution (parameter : Value) (captures : Nat → Value) : Nat → Value
  | 0 => parameter
  | n + 1 => captures n

theorem close_parameter_body [DecidableEq K] {arena : Arena K D} {env : Nat}
    {store : Nat → Option Value} {layout : Layout K} {values : List Value}
    (success : realize arena env store layout = some values)
    (cells : CellsTyped arena env store layout) (filler : Value)
    {parameter : Value} {a result : Ty} (hp : ValueTyped emptyContext parameter a)
    {body : TypedCall.Comp} (hb : TypedCall.CompTyped (Original.extend (context layout) a) body result) :
    TypedCall.CompTyped emptyContext
      (substituteCallComp (parameterSubstitution parameter (substitution filler values)) body) result := by
  apply substituteCallComp_typed hb
  intro i ty hi
  cases i with
  | zero =>
      simp only [Original.extend, Option.some.injEq] at hi
      subst ty
      exact hp
  | succ i => exact realized_substitution_typed success cells filler i ty hi

/-- Computation entry retains the actual closed delayed body, at UA. -/
theorem delayed_parameter {body : TypedCall.Comp} {a : Ty}
    (h : TypedCall.CompTyped emptyContext body a) :
    ValueTyped emptyContext (.delay body) (.thunk a) := .delay h

theorem close_computation_body [DecidableEq K] {arena : Arena K D} {env : Nat}
    {store : Nat → Option Value} {layout : Layout K} {values : List Value}
    (success : realize arena env store layout = some values)
    (cells : CellsTyped arena env store layout) (filler : Value)
    {argument body : TypedCall.Comp} {a result : Ty}
    (ha : TypedCall.CompTyped emptyContext argument a)
    (hb : TypedCall.CompTyped (Original.extend (context layout) (.thunk a)) body result) :
    TypedCall.CompTyped emptyContext
      (substituteCallComp
        (parameterSubstitution (.delay argument) (substitution filler values)) body) result :=
  close_parameter_body success cells filler (.delay ha) hb

example : realize (Arena.root ()) 0 (fun _ => (none : Option Value))
    [((Reference.lexical (1 : Nat)), Ty.base .unit)] = none := rfl

example : realize (Arena.root ()) 0 (fun _ => (none : Option Value))
    [((Reference.global (K := Nat) 3), Ty.base .unit)] = none := rfl

example : realize (Arena.root ()) 0 (fun _ => some (Value.original .unit))
    [((Reference.global (K := Nat) 3), Ty.base .unit)] =
      some [.original .unit] := rfl

end YulangClosure.CallEnvironmentRealization

# Native closure environments, current cells and represented body realization

Status: source correspondence candidate, pending combined formal/source review.
Authors: primary /root (source/verification) and constructive author
/root/native_closure_environment_astra_r1 (formal candidate).
Baseline657d688fc022261fa1013f7eb4f2b323d6cfd4a6, research/simple-sub-intrusion.
Contract LEAN-NATIVE-CLOSURE-ENVIRONMENT-20261025/r1 SHA
2630ec7db277777bf4e0fb8e99a665cdd65d842471264a736a079c122a1f073f.
All59 pinned inputs match. Requested childAstra/medium, observedUNKNOWN.

## Authority and exact claim

The existing operational specification requires the typing context to retain
captures/shared resources (tex206), distinguishes Value formal A from Computation
formal UA (220-221), and permits a finite environment graph read as closed
substitution (258-261). This note derives the native lexical-address supplier
and uses the companion formal construction to close represented Call bodies.
It adds no language semantics, executable callable constructor or compiler change.

The environment graph, cell store and value/closure graph are distinct objects.
A closure stores an environment index, not a copy of its bound values. Environment
nodes are immutable once appended; a binder resolves to a stable cell address.
Reading that cell observes its CURRENT content, which may be uninitialized or
have been written since closure capture. A recursive local can produce a cycle
cell -> closure -> captured environment -> same cell even though environment
parent edges are acyclic. Parent acyclicity proves neither guarded value-graph
realization nor a typed store. Those original obligations remain OPEN.

For every actually generated finite environment arena and valid saved environment,
lookup terminates and returns the nearest matching full binder identity's cell.
Later arena appends do not change that old address resolution. Dispatch-only
nodes leave lexical resolution unchanged. Parameter binding shadows precisely
its full identity. Native closure entry uses the saved environment, independent
of the caller's environment except for explicitly retained dispatch/value data.
For a finite resolved layout whose current cells already have represented typed
values, the formal realization constructs the exact substitution and applies the
existing body substitution theorem. This last result remains conditional on
source layout and actual value representation/typing; it does not create those
premises from an arbitrary native store.

## All environment constructors and handle validity

Environment at machine175 retains parent Option<usize>, optional (Binder,cell)
and dispatch::State. Machine start447 creates exactly node0 with parent=None,
binder=None and default dispatch. Existing environments are never overwritten,
removed or truncated. The only production pushes are:

| Owner | New node and returned handle |
| --- | --- |
| with_dispatch2596-2599 | id=old length; parent=Some(input), binder=None, supplied dispatch; return id. |
| extend2626-2633 | id=old length; parent=Some(input), binder=Some(exact key,cell), copy parent's dispatch; return id. |
| bind2635-2638 | id=old cell length; append Some(exact ReceivedValue); then extend(input,key,id). |

All non-root environment handles originate from these returned pre-append lengths.
All other uses copy existing handles from active Evaluate state, saved frames,
Closure/Delay payloads, or use literal0 for root evaluation/initialization.
No source integer, arithmetic-derived value or caller-provided raw index becomes
an environment handle. These fields are private. Test-only hand-written machine
states are outside the production constructor induction.

Inductively, input handles are below the old arena length, and every newly
created parent is strictly below its child's new index. Earlier nodes are
unchanged. Reusing any older valid environment as parent is permitted; the graph
is not a single contiguous chain and does not require parent=child-1. Root is
parentless; every source-produced non-root node has an older parent. Thus every
lookup's followed parent chain is finite. Vector reallocation does not invalidate
index handles. Successful returned allocations are modeled; an infallible native
allocation abort is not claimed to return a recoverable error.

This is a source construction induction over the complete handle-producer set,
not an assumed arbitrary well-formed arena. The model's own append theorems
supply that invariant for all histories of such constructors, retaining dispatch
and binder/cell payloads. A malformed self-parent/cyclic arena is not a producer
result and cannot instantiate the builder theorem.

## Actual lookup, identity and module cells

Machine.lookup2585-2594 first checks the selected frame via get. If its binder
exists and the supplied predicate matches, it returns that cell immediately.
Otherwise it follows parent; a missing frame or absent parent returns None.
For generated valid environments, strict parent decrease makes the unbounded
Rust loop coincide with the finite formal lookup, including exact nearest match.
The finite bound counts environment nodes, including binderless dispatch nodes;
it does not bound later user computation or resolving value-graph cycles.

Binder at program207-211 is a tagged union of Parameter(HirParameterId),
Local(HirLocalId), and Catch(LocalSourceCatchBinderId). Name785-811 uses:

| Source resolution | Exact address lookup |
| --- | --- |
| ModuleDef(id) | definition_indices.get(full id), independent of lexical env. |
| Parameter(id) | nearest Binder::Parameter(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| Local(id) | nearest Binder::Local(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| CatchBinder(id) or CaseBinder(id) | nearest Binder::Catch(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| Imported, Unresolved, Ambiguous | no address; MissingBinding. |

HirParameterId compares source-root owner and ordinal (module1377-1408);
HirLocalId likewise retains its owner and ordinal. Catch identity additionally
retains arm_source (local_source463ff). The tags remain distinct; equal spelling,
ordinal alone, source display or hash collision is not equality. The formal key
must denote these complete identities, or an injective encoding already supplied
elsewhere. Its decidable equality is not a new spelling-based resolution policy.

Program994 and1008 set each definition index to definitions.len() immediately
before pushing that definition. Machine452 allocates exactly definitions.len()
initial cells, all None. Each stored module index is therefore in bounds; later
cell appends preserve it. Global resolution is a direct cell reference in a
resolved layout, not a fake lexical binder inserted into environment0. Missing
module ids remain failures. This address fact does not establish source-to-layout
coverage for arbitrary expressions or native cell typing.

After address resolution, Name814 reads self.cells[cell]. Missing lexical
address yields MissingBinding; present lexical cell with None yields
UninitializedBinding. Module cell None starts guarded lazy global initialization,
with a GlobalRead frame and initializer environment derived from0; repeated active
initialization yields RecursiveDefinitionInitialization. No placeholder value is
returned for an absent/uninitialized binding.

On Some(received), dispatch_name may update the copied ReceivedValue.dispatch,
then consume uses NameConsumption and may return or execute a computation.
The current-cell realization denotes the stored carrier before these operations;
address lookup transparency is not dispatch or force semantic transparency.
Neither dispatch_name nor consume writes the stored cell in this path.

## Dispatch-only nodes and error boundaries

initializer_environment2601 returns the same parent when dictionaries are absent;
otherwise it calls dispatch.initializer and appends a binderless node with the
returned state. substitute_environment2606 is a no-op if dictionaries or the
substitution are absent; otherwise it composes dispatch.substitution with the
supplied substitution and appends a binderless node. dispatch_environment2612
appends a dispatch word and likewise creates a binderless node. These wrappers
therefore preserve every lexical address on success, including nested wrappers.
Their dispatch values are retained, not erased as semantically irrelevant.

The called dispatch owner is dispatch.rs: append67, then78, initializer143,
name161. These helpers mutate their own metadata arenas/default map, never the
lexical environment nodes or cell contents. A returned error before with_dispatch
means no lexical node was appended. It does NOT mean global rollback:
initializer inserts into defaults before rejecting an existing entry, and name
can append metadata before a later allocation failure. No proof here asserts
idempotence, commutativity, freshness or observational irrelevance of those
substitutions. Their ordered semantic interpretation is a separate obligation.

## Closure capture and actual entry branches

Instruction::Lambda864-887 copies parameter, pattern flags, role, schemas, body
label and CURRENT environment into ExecutableValue::Closure. Callee1181-1200
creates the delayed argument with the CALLER environment before examining the
callee. The Closure pattern1224-1232 then binds its environment variable to the
SAVED closure environment. At1286 substitute_environment receives that saved
index and the callee ReceivedValue.dispatch; the caller's lexical environment is
not substituted for it. The delay still refers to caller environment, which is
correct argument scope, rather than a change to the closure body scope.

new_invocation runs before substitution; a later dispatch failure can retain
owner/metadata changes while body entry fails. The address theorem neither
reorders these steps nor asserts whole-machine rollback or typed error-freedom.
ReceiverReturn/ValueEntry carry the resulting saved-derived environment exactly.

| Entry branch | Lexical effect |
| --- | --- |
| Computation1316-1331 | Bind the closure parameter to the same delay handle, Computation interface, selected receiving view, dispatch=None; evaluate body without forcing it here. This branch does not inspect unit/record flags. |
| Value ordinary1440-1490 | Force argument first. After optional callback validation/view construction, bind parameter to exact returned value/view/dispatch with Value interface, then evaluate body. |
| Value unit1471-1476 | Validate actual Unit; retain saved-derived environment without a parameter binder. Failure enters no body. |
| Value record1468 / bind_record_parameter2655 | Process fields in source order; bind each field identity only when its value/default has been obtained. No whole-record parameter binder is added here. |

Optional callback_schema validation may fail before any parameter binding; on
success it changes the copied receiving view while retaining the actual value
and dispatch. The body-closing lemma must use that actual carrier's representation,
not an invented unchanged-view premise. For Computation, a represented argument
is a delay with a typed computation body; it is not an eagerly evaluated result.

bind_record_parameter first validates the argument/view and actual record. A
present field projects its view, composes its dispatch with the argument dispatch,
sets Value interface and creates a fresh parameter cell. If absent with a default,
it saves RecordDefault and evaluates the default under the environment containing
only earlier fields. On return1491, the default value/view is projected, that
field is bound, then processing resumes at index+1. Missing without default,
invalid record/view or projection failure does not silently introduce a binding.
Even empty patterns require an actual record. A default may suspend/fail/diverge;
no theorem here claims finite completion of all defaults. Repeated application
of the append lookup theorem applies to each successful field introduction.

## Cell allocation/writes and all other binder producers

There is no cell removal or index reuse. The complete production cell mutation
set found by searching every self.cells occurrence is:

| Owner | Mutation and environment relation |
| --- | --- |
| Start452 | Allocate None for every global definition. |
| begin_local2523-2526 | Append fresh None; recursive local extends env before initializer, nonrecursive does not yet extend. |
| Frame::Local1543-1560 | Write actual received carrier with Value interface; recursive env already contains the cell, nonrecursive extends now; continue the block. |
| Frame::Root1739 | Write received carrier with Value interface into scheduled definition cell. |
| Frame::GlobalRead1760 | Write received carrier with Value interface into lazily initialized global cell; then dispatch/consume a copy. |
| bind2637 | Append Some(exact supplied carrier), then extend with its fresh cell. |

The structural store theorem intentionally permits current-cell changes; it
does not claim that the runtime rewrites every initialized cell arbitrarily or
that every write preserves a source type. Recursive closure capture can occur
while its own preallocated cell is None; later initialization changes what the
same captured address reads. Before that write the partial realization must
fail; after it the same address can return the new value. The finite Call value
syntax cannot generally represent that cyclic closure graph, which remains OPEN.

All bind callers use the same constructor law: CatchReturn value arm1116;
Computation formal1316; ordinary Value formal1476; RecordDefault1494;
Case binder1699 and structural-case list1717; request payload2194 and continuation
binder2216; record field2671. The only direct extend callers besides bind are
recursive preallocation2526 and nonrecursive local completion1553. Wildcards,
unit catch payload and patterns with no binder retain the input environment.
A forwarded handler's stored environment is copied by template replay; the
reviewed template result does not mutate that environment arena or cell store.

## Formal realization application and residual source owners

The exact final APIs and their source instantiation are recorded after author
handoff and Lean verification. The required construction is partial lookup of
each resolved capture, current represented cell read, and an indexed finite
substitution whose typed indices match those reads. Only out-of-domain indices
may carry an irrelevant total-function filler. Successful realization alone
establishes value identity/coverage, not type: per-cell ValueTyped evidence must
supply the original context's declared types, including duplicate/aliased cells.
The body result then follows by the existing substituteCallComp_typed theorem,
with the constructed premise rather than an assumed typed substitution object.

Remaining owners, all primary intake:
- ENV-LAYOUT-1: actual source-resolved binder/global references and de Bruijn free
  positions for each represented body, with binder lifting and coverage.
- ENV-CELL-VALUE-1: native ReceivedValue/current cell -> represented TypedCall.Value
  and its original type; primitive literal readback is only one accepted supplier.
- ENV-GRAPH-1: guarded recursive/shared value graph realization and original typing.
- ENV-CALLABLE-1: closure as a value, full code/environment/adapter/native trace
  interpretation; current Function is outside Value and is not silently inserted.
- ENV-DISPATCH-1: source dictionary dispatch and consumption/force meaning,
  including receiving/view metadata and operation errors.

The full source-native / typed callable parent therefore remains OPEN. This
packet supplies the concrete address/current-cell/substitution mechanism and its
conditional typed body application, not arbitrary source typing or Bad exclusion.
NO_SAFE_CODE_SLICE; no confirmed runtime defect. No compiler, diagnostic,
expectation, config, native test or new production semantics change is made.

## Authority and exact claim

The existing operational specification requires the typing context to retain
captures/shared resources (tex206), distinguishes Value formal A from Computation
formal UA (220-221), and permits a finite environment graph read as closed
substitution (258-261). This note derives the native lexical-address supplier
and uses the companion formal construction to close represented Call bodies.
It adds no language semantics, executable callable constructor or compiler change.

The environment graph, cell store and value/closure graph are distinct objects.
A closure stores an environment index, not a copy of its bound values. Environment
nodes are immutable once appended; a binder resolves to a stable cell address.
Reading that cell observes its CURRENT content, which may be uninitialized or
have been written since closure capture. A recursive local can produce a cycle
cell -> closure -> captured environment -> same cell even though environment
parent edges are acyclic. Parent acyclicity proves neither guarded value-graph
realization nor a typed store. Those original obligations remain OPEN.

For every actually generated finite environment arena and valid saved environment,
lookup terminates and returns the nearest matching full binder identity's cell.
Later arena appends do not change that old address resolution. Dispatch-only
nodes leave lexical resolution unchanged. Parameter binding shadows precisely
its full identity. Native closure entry uses the saved environment, independent
of the caller's environment except for explicitly retained dispatch/value data.
For a finite resolved layout whose current cells already have represented typed
values, the formal realization constructs the exact substitution and applies the
existing body substitution theorem. This last result remains conditional on
source layout and actual value representation/typing; it does not create those
premises from an arbitrary native store.

and dispatch::State. Machine start447 creates exactly node0 with parent=None,

| Owner | New node and returned handle |
| --- | --- |

All non-root environment handles originate from these returned pre-append lengths.
All other uses copy existing handles from active Evaluate state, saved frames,
Closure/Delay payloads, or use literal0 for root evaluation/initialization.
No source integer, arithmetic-derived value or caller-provided raw index becomes
an environment handle. These fields are private. Test-only hand-written machine
states are outside the production constructor induction.

Inductively, input handles are below the old arena length, and every newly
created parent is strictly below its child's new index. Earlier nodes are
unchanged. Reusing any older valid environment as parent is permitted; the graph
is not a single contiguous chain and does not require parent=child-1. Root is
parentless; every source-produced non-root node has an older parent. Thus every
lookup's followed parent chain is finite. Vector reallocation does not invalidate
index handles. Successful returned allocations are modeled; an infallible native
allocation abort is not claimed to return a recoverable error.

This is a source construction induction over the complete handle-producer set,
not an assumed arbitrary well-formed arena. The model's own append theorems
supply that invariant for all histories of such constructors, retaining dispatch
and binder/cell payloads. A malformed self-parent/cyclic arena is not a producer
result and cannot instantiate the builder theorem.

## Actual lookup, identity and module cells

Machine.lookup2585-2594 first checks the selected frame via get. If its binder
exists and the supplied predicate matches, it returns that cell immediately.
Otherwise it follows parent; a missing frame or absent parent returns None.
For generated valid environments, strict parent decrease makes the unbounded
Rust loop coincide with the finite formal lookup, including exact nearest match.
The finite bound counts environment nodes, including binderless dispatch nodes;
it does not bound later user computation or resolving value-graph cycles.

Binder at program207-211 is a tagged union of Parameter(HirParameterId),
Local(HirLocalId), and Catch(LocalSourceCatchBinderId). Name785-811 uses:

| Source resolution | Exact address lookup |
| --- | --- |
| ModuleDef(id) | definition_indices.get(full id), independent of lexical env. |
| Parameter(id) | nearest Binder::Parameter(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| Local(id) | nearest Binder::Local(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| CatchBinder(id) or CaseBinder(id) | nearest Binder::Catch(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| Imported, Unresolved, Ambiguous | no address; MissingBinding. |

HirParameterId compares source-root owner and ordinal (module1377-1408);
HirLocalId likewise retains its owner and ordinal. Catch identity additionally
retains arm_source (local_source463ff). The tags remain distinct; equal spelling,
ordinal alone, source display or hash collision is not equality. The formal key
must denote these complete identities, or an injective encoding already supplied
elsewhere. Its decidable equality is not a new spelling-based resolution policy.

Program994 and1008 set each definition index to definitions.len() immediately
before pushing that definition. Machine452 allocates exactly definitions.len()

cell appends preserve it. Global resolution is a direct cell reference in a
resolved layout, not a fake lexical binder inserted into environment0. Missing
module ids remain failures. This address fact does not establish source-to-layout
coverage for arbitrary expressions or native cell typing.

After address resolution, Name814 reads self.cells[cell]. Missing lexical
address yields MissingBinding; present lexical cell with None yields

with a GlobalRead frame and initializer environment derived from0; repeated active

returned for an absent/uninitialized binding.

On Some(received), dispatch_name may update the copied ReceivedValue.dispatch,

The current-cell realization denotes the stored carrier before these operations;

## Dispatch-only nodes and error boundaries

initializer_environment2601 returns the same parent when dictionaries are absent;
otherwise it calls dispatch.initializer and appends a binderless node with the
returned state. substitute_environment2606 is a no-op if dictionaries or the
substitution are absent; otherwise it composes dispatch.substitution with the
supplied substitution and appends a binderless node. dispatch_environment2612
appends a dispatch word and likewise creates a binderless node. These wrappers
therefore preserve every lexical address on success, including nested wrappers.
Their dispatch values are retained, not erased as semantically irrelevant.

The called dispatch owner is dispatch.rs: append67, then78, initializer143,
name161. These helpers mutate their own metadata arenas/default map, never the
lexical environment nodes or cell contents. A returned error before with_dispatch
means no lexical node was appended. It does NOT mean global rollback:
initializer inserts into defaults before rejecting an existing entry, and name
can append metadata before a later allocation failure. No proof here asserts
idempotence, commutativity, freshness or observational irrelevance of those
substitutions. Their ordered semantic interpretation is a separate obligation.

## Closure capture and actual entry branches

Instruction::Lambda864-887 copies parameter, pattern flags, role, schemas, body
label and CURRENT environment into ExecutableValue::Closure. Callee1181-1200
creates the delayed argument with the CALLER environment before examining the
callee. The Closure pattern1224-1232 then binds its environment variable to the
SAVED closure environment. At1286 substitute_environment receives that saved
index and the callee ReceivedValue.dispatch; the caller's lexical environment is
not substituted for it. The delay still refers to caller environment, which is
correct argument scope, rather than a change to the closure body scope.

new_invocation runs before substitution; a later dispatch failure can retain
owner/metadata changes while body entry fails. The address theorem neither
reorders these steps nor asserts whole-machine rollback or typed error-freedom.
ReceiverReturn/ValueEntry carry the resulting saved-derived environment exactly.

| Entry branch | Lexical effect |
| --- | --- |
| Computation1316-1331 | Bind the closure parameter to the same delay handle, Computation interface, selected receiving view, dispatch=None; evaluate body without forcing it here. This branch does not inspect unit/record flags. |
| Value ordinary1440-1490 | Force argument first. After optional callback validation/view construction, bind parameter to exact returned value/view/dispatch with Value interface, then evaluate body. |
| Value unit1471-1476 | Validate actual Unit; retain saved-derived environment without a parameter binder. Failure enters no body. |
| Value record1468 / bind_record_parameter2655 | Process fields in source order; bind each field identity only when its value/default has been obtained. No whole-record parameter binder is added here. |

Optional callback_schema validation may fail before any parameter binding; on
success it changes the copied receiving view while retaining the actual value
and dispatch. The body-closing lemma must use that actual carrier's representation,
not an invented unchanged-view premise. For Computation, a represented argument
is a delay with a typed computation body; it is not an eagerly evaluated result.

bind_record_parameter first validates the argument/view and actual record. A
present field projects its view, composes its dispatch with the argument dispatch,
sets Value interface and creates a fresh parameter cell. If absent with a default,
it saves RecordDefault and evaluates the default under the environment containing
only earlier fields. On return1491, the default value/view is projected, that
field is bound, then processing resumes at index+1. Missing without default,
invalid record/view or projection failure does not silently introduce a binding.
Even empty patterns require an actual record. A default may suspend/fail/diverge;
no theorem here claims finite completion of all defaults. Repeated application
of the append lookup theorem applies to each successful field introduction.

## Cell allocation/writes and all other binder producers

There is no cell removal or index reuse. The complete production cell mutation
set found by searching every self.cells occurrence is:

| Owner | Mutation and environment relation |
| --- | --- |
| Start452 | Allocate None for every global definition. |
| begin_local2523-2526 | Append fresh None; recursive local extends env before initializer, nonrecursive does not yet extend. |
| Frame::Local1543-1560 | Write actual received carrier with Value interface; recursive env already contains the cell, nonrecursive extends now; continue the block. |
| Frame::Root1739 | Write received carrier with Value interface into scheduled definition cell. |
| Frame::GlobalRead1760 | Write received carrier with Value interface into lazily initialized global cell; then dispatch/consume a copy. |
| bind2637 | Append Some(exact supplied carrier), then extend with its fresh cell. |

The structural store theorem intentionally permits current-cell changes; it
does not claim that the runtime rewrites every initialized cell arbitrarily or
that every write preserves a source type. Recursive closure capture can occur
while its own preallocated cell is None; later initialization changes what the
same captured address reads. Before that write the partial realization must
fail; after it the same address can return the new value. The finite Call value
syntax cannot generally represent that cyclic closure graph, which remains OPEN.

All bind callers use the same constructor law: CatchReturn value arm1116;
Computation formal1316; ordinary Value formal1476; RecordDefault1494;
Case binder1699 and structural-case list1717; request payload2194 and continuation
binder2216; record field2671. The only direct extend callers besides bind are
recursive preallocation2526 and nonrecursive local completion1553. Wildcards,
unit catch payload and patterns with no binder retain the input environment.
A forwarded handler's stored environment is copied by template replay; the
reviewed template result does not mutate that environment arena or cell store.

## Formal realization application and residual source owners

The exact final APIs and their source instantiation are recorded after author
handoff and Lean verification. The required construction is partial lookup of
each resolved capture, current represented cell read, and an indexed finite
substitution whose typed indices match those reads. Only out-of-domain indices
may carry an irrelevant total-function filler. Successful realization alone
establishes value identity/coverage, not type: per-cell ValueTyped evidence must
supply the original context's declared types, including duplicate/aliased cells.
The body result then follows by the existing substituteCallComp_typed theorem,
with the constructed premise rather than an assumed typed substitution object.

Remaining owners, all primary intake:
- ENV-LAYOUT-1: actual source-resolved binder/global references and de Bruijn free
  positions for each represented body, with binder lifting and coverage.
- ENV-CELL-VALUE-1: native ReceivedValue/current cell -> represented TypedCall.Value
  and its original type; primitive literal readback is only one accepted supplier.
- ENV-GRAPH-1: guarded recursive/shared value graph realization and original typing.
- ENV-CALLABLE-1: closure as a value, full code/environment/adapter/native trace
  interpretation; current Function is outside Value and is not silently inserted.
- ENV-DISPATCH-1: source dictionary dispatch and consumption/force meaning,
  including receiving/view metadata and operation errors.

The full source-native / typed callable parent therefore remains OPEN. This

source_note_text:
# Native closure environments, current cells and represented body realization

Status: source correspondence candidate, pending combined formal/source review.
Authors: primary /root (source/verification) and constructive author
/root/native_closure_environment_astra_r1 (formal candidate).
Baseline657d688fc022261fa1013f7eb4f2b323d6cfd4a6, research/simple-sub-intrusion.
Contract LEAN-NATIVE-CLOSURE-ENVIRONMENT-20261025/r1 SHA
2630ec7db277777bf4e0fb8e99a665cdd65d842471264a736a079c122a1f073f.
All59 pinned inputs match. Requested childAstra/medium, observedUNKNOWN.

## Authority and exact claim

The existing operational specification requires the typing context to retain
captures/shared resources (tex206), distinguishes Value formal A from Computation
formal UA (220-221), and permits a finite environment graph read as closed
substitution (258-261). This note derives the native lexical-address supplier
and uses the companion formal construction to close represented Call bodies.
It adds no language semantics, executable callable constructor or compiler change.

The environment graph, cell store and value/closure graph are distinct objects.
A closure stores an environment index, not a copy of its bound values. Environment
nodes are immutable once appended; a binder resolves to a stable cell address.
Reading that cell observes its CURRENT content, which may be uninitialized or
have been written since closure capture. A recursive local can produce a cycle
cell -> closure -> captured environment -> same cell even though environment
parent edges are acyclic. Parent acyclicity proves neither guarded value-graph
realization nor a typed store. Those original obligations remain OPEN.

For every actually generated finite environment arena and valid saved environment,
lookup terminates and returns the nearest matching full binder identity's cell.
Later arena appends do not change that old address resolution. Dispatch-only
nodes leave lexical resolution unchanged. Parameter binding shadows precisely
its full identity. Native closure entry uses the saved environment, independent
of the caller's environment except for explicitly retained dispatch/value data.
For a finite resolved layout whose current cells already have represented typed
values, the formal realization constructs the exact substitution and applies the
existing body substitution theorem. This last result remains conditional on
source layout and actual value representation/typing; it does not create those
premises from an arbitrary native store.

## All environment constructors and handle validity

Environment at machine175 retains parent Option<usize>, optional (Binder,cell)
and dispatch::State. Machine start447 creates exactly node0 with parent=None,
binder=None and default dispatch. Existing environments are never overwritten,
removed or truncated. The only production pushes are:

| Owner | New node and returned handle |
| --- | --- |
| with_dispatch2596-2599 | id=old length; parent=Some(input), binder=None, supplied dispatch; return id. |
| extend2626-2633 | id=old length; parent=Some(input), binder=Some(exact key,cell), copy parent's dispatch; return id. |
| bind2635-2638 | id=old cell length; append Some(exact ReceivedValue); then extend(input,key,id). |

All non-root environment handles originate from these returned pre-append lengths.
All other uses copy existing handles from active Evaluate state, saved frames,
Closure/Delay payloads, or use literal0 for root evaluation/initialization.
No source integer, arithmetic-derived value or caller-provided raw index becomes
an environment handle. These fields are private. Test-only hand-written machine
states are outside the production constructor induction.

Inductively, input handles are below the old arena length, and every newly
created parent is strictly below its child's new index. Earlier nodes are
unchanged. Reusing any older valid environment as parent is permitted; the graph
is not a single contiguous chain and does not require parent=child-1. Root is
parentless; every source-produced non-root node has an older parent. Thus every
lookup's followed parent chain is finite. Vector reallocation does not invalidate
index handles. Successful returned allocations are modeled; an infallible native
allocation abort is not claimed to return a recoverable error.

This is a source construction induction over the complete handle-producer set,
not an assumed arbitrary well-formed arena. The model's own append theorems
supply that invariant for all histories of such constructors, retaining dispatch
and binder/cell payloads. A malformed self-parent/cyclic arena is not a producer
result and cannot instantiate the builder theorem.

## Actual lookup, identity and module cells

Machine.lookup2585-2594 first checks the selected frame via get. If its binder
exists and the supplied predicate matches, it returns that cell immediately.
Otherwise it follows parent; a missing frame or absent parent returns None.
For generated valid environments, strict parent decrease makes the unbounded
Rust loop coincide with the finite formal lookup, including exact nearest match.
The finite bound counts environment nodes, including binderless dispatch nodes;
it does not bound later user computation or resolving value-graph cycles.

Binder at program207-211 is a tagged union of Parameter(HirParameterId),
Local(HirLocalId), and Catch(LocalSourceCatchBinderId). Name785-811 uses:

| Source resolution | Exact address lookup |
| --- | --- |
| ModuleDef(id) | definition_indices.get(full id), independent of lexical env. |
| Parameter(id) | nearest Binder::Parameter(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| Local(id) | nearest Binder::Local(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| CatchBinder(id) or CaseBinder(id) | nearest Binder::Catch(candidate) with candidate==id. |
| Imported, Unresolved, Ambiguous | no address; MissingBinding. |

HirParameterId compares source-root owner and ordinal (module1377-1408);
HirLocalId likewise retains its owner and ordinal. Catch identity additionally
retains arm_source (local_source463ff). The tags remain distinct; equal spelling,
ordinal alone, source display or hash collision is not equality. The formal key
must denote these complete identities, or an injective encoding already supplied
elsewhere. Its decidable equality is not a new spelling-based resolution policy.

Program994 and1008 set each definition index to definitions.len() immediately
before pushing that definition. Machine452 allocates exactly definitions.len()
initial cells, all None. Each stored module index is therefore in bounds; later
cell appends preserve it. Global resolution is a direct cell reference in a
resolved layout, not a fake lexical binder inserted into environment0. Missing
module ids remain failures. This address fact does not establish source-to-layout
coverage for arbitrary expressions or native cell typing.

After address resolution, Name814 reads self.cells[cell]. Missing lexical
address yields MissingBinding; present lexical cell with None yields
UninitializedBinding. Module cell None starts guarded lazy global initialization,
with a GlobalRead frame and initializer environment derived from0; repeated active
initialization yields RecursiveDefinitionInitialization. No placeholder value is
returned for an absent/uninitialized binding.

On Some(received), dispatch_name may update the copied ReceivedValue.dispatch,
then consume uses NameConsumption and may return or execute a computation.
The current-cell realization denotes the stored carrier before these operations;
address lookup transparency is not dispatch or force semantic transparency.
Neither dispatch_name nor consume writes the stored cell in this path.

## Dispatch-only nodes and error boundaries

initializer_environment2601 returns the same parent when dictionaries are absent;
otherwise it calls dispatch.initializer and appends a binderless node with the
returned state. substitute_environment2606 is a no-op if dictionaries or the
substitution are absent; otherwise it composes dispatch.substitution with the
supplied substitution and appends a binderless node. dispatch_environment2612
appends a dispatch word and likewise creates a binderless node. These wrappers
therefore preserve every lexical address on success, including nested wrappers.
Their dispatch values are retained, not erased as semantically irrelevant.

The called dispatch owner is dispatch.rs: append67, then78, initializer143,
name161. These helpers mutate their own metadata arenas/default map, never the
lexical environment nodes or cell contents. A returned error before with_dispatch
means no lexical node was appended. It does NOT mean global rollback:
initializer inserts into defaults before rejecting an existing entry, and name
can append metadata before a later allocation failure. No proof here asserts
idempotence, commutativity, freshness or observational irrelevance of those
substitutions. Their ordered semantic interpretation is a separate obligation.

## Closure capture and actual entry branches

Instruction::Lambda864-887 copies parameter, pattern flags, role, schemas, body
label and CURRENT environment into ExecutableValue::Closure. Callee1181-1200
creates the delayed argument with the CALLER environment before examining the
callee. The Closure pattern1224-1232 then binds its environment variable to the
SAVED closure environment. At1286 substitute_environment receives that saved
index and the callee ReceivedValue.dispatch; the caller's lexical environment is
not substituted for it. The delay still refers to caller environment, which is
correct argument scope, rather than a change to the closure body scope.

new_invocation runs before substitution; a later dispatch failure can retain
owner/metadata changes while body entry fails. The address theorem neither
reorders these steps nor asserts whole-machine rollback or typed error-freedom.
ReceiverReturn/ValueEntry carry the resulting saved-derived environment exactly.

| Entry branch | Lexical effect |
| --- | --- |
| Computation1316-1331 | Bind the closure parameter to the same delay handle, Computation interface, selected receiving view, dispatch=None; evaluate body without forcing it here. This branch does not inspect unit/record flags. |
| Value ordinary1440-1490 | Force argument first. After optional callback validation/view construction, bind parameter to exact returned value/view/dispatch with Value interface, then evaluate body. |
| Value unit1471-1476 | Validate actual Unit; retain saved-derived environment without a parameter binder. Failure enters no body. |
| Value record1468 / bind_record_parameter2655 | Process fields in source order; bind each field identity only when its value/default has been obtained. No whole-record parameter binder is added here. |

Optional callback_schema validation may fail before any parameter binding; on
success it changes the copied receiving view while retaining the actual value
and dispatch. The body-closing lemma must use that actual carrier's representation,
not an invented unchanged-view premise. For Computation, a represented argument
is a delay with a typed computation body; it is not an eagerly evaluated result.

bind_record_parameter first validates the argument/view and actual record. A
present field projects its view, composes its dispatch with the argument dispatch,
sets Value interface and creates a fresh parameter cell. If absent with a default,
it saves RecordDefault and evaluates the default under the environment containing
only earlier fields. On return1491, the default value/view is projected, that

Even empty patterns require an actual record. A default may suspend/fail/diverge;

of the append lookup theorem applies to each successful field introduction.

## Cell allocation/writes and all other binder producers

There is no cell removal or index reuse. The complete production cell mutation
set found by searching every self.cells occurrence is:

| Owner | Mutation and environment relation |
| --- | --- |
| Start452 | Allocate None for every global definition. |
| begin_local2523-2526 | Append fresh None; recursive local extends env before initializer, nonrecursive does not yet extend. |
| Frame::Local1543-1560 | Write actual received carrier with Value interface; recursive env already contains the cell, nonrecursive extends now; continue the block. |
| Frame::Root1739 | Write received carrier with Value interface into scheduled definition cell. |
| Frame::GlobalRead1760 | Write received carrier with Value interface into lazily initialized global cell; then dispatch/consume a copy. |
| bind2637 | Append Some(exact supplied carrier), then extend with its fresh cell. |

The structural store theorem intentionally permits current-cell changes; it

that every write preserves a source type. Recursive closure capture can occur
while its own preallocated cell is None; later initialization changes what the
same captured address reads. Before that write the partial realization must

reviewed template result does not mutate that environment arena or cell store.

The exact final APIs and their source instantiation are recorded after author

- ENV-CELL-VALUE-1: native ReceivedValue/current cell -> represented TypedCall.Value

- ENV-DISPATCH-1: source dictionary dispatch and consumption/force meaning,
